answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, auditable stake rather than the number of agent accounts. For example, require each agent to lock a deposit and earn voting weight only through work that independent counterparties verify; proven fraud forfeits the deposit and can void its rewards. An attacker may plant a terrace of identities across an orchard of tasks, but each must be funded and sustained, while a shared anchor of control risks exposing the whole cluster. Creating more names no longer creates cheap influence.
